findings.description: Every piece of audio evidence (all Python tests, T-200/T-201, demos, blind pairs, pilot and listening gates) is produced by folk-render driving the core directly. The shipped VST3 is exercised only by T-302 (one note-on at offset 17 makes sound; state round trip; editor) and pluginval, and T-302 compiles FolkProcessor.cpp into a console program and feeds a MidiBuffer straight into processBlock, bypassing the VST3 layer. Parameter unit conversion, pitch wheel, CC 1/2/11/64, all-notes-off, chunking of oversized blocks and latency reporting in the plugin are verified by nothing.
findings.lens: technical correctness (tests pass while the product is wrong); integration
findings.conditions: one mapping slip in FolkProcessor.cpp: normalised JUCE values (0..1) handed to Engine::setParam instead of engine units, pitch wheel 0..16383 not centred, CC 2/11/64 not forwarded, or JUCE_VST3_EMULATE_MIDI_CC_WITH_PARAMETERS set to 0 (in VST3, pitch bend and CCs reach a plugin only through that emulation)
findings.root_cause: the test architecture treats the core as the product; the wrapper is assumed to be a thin pass-through
findings.traces_to: D-094, D-092; S-310 Done when; T-302; tests/juce/host_test.cpp; S-LISTEN (demos rendered by folk-render); lesson L-20261008T173530Z (assert through the real processor)
findings.failure_path: S-310 passes on ctest (five HostTests: one note sounds) and five .vst3 bundles existing; S-320 passes on pluginval's 20 log checks, which check host-contract rules, not musical behaviour; S-LISTEN judges folk-render audio. A wrapper that sends normalised values to the engine plays a4_hz at 415 Hz (about 100 cents flat) and harmonica bends or breath controllers do nothing in Ableton Live, and every Done when still passes.
findings.mitigation: Add a frozen host test T-303 per plugin: drive the wrapper with the events of the five standard demo scripts (note, pitch wheel, CC 1, 2, 11, 64, 120, 123, parameter changes set through the JUCE parameters in engine units, a block larger than the prepared size) and compare its output, shifted by latencySamples(), with folk-render's output for the same events within 1e-4; add a CI step that loads the built .vst3 bundle through juce::VST3PluginFormat (not the source) and sends pitch bend and CC 2 through the VST3 interface, asserting the pitch and level change; ask the owner at each G-L gate to play the plugin in the assumed host (bend, breath controller).
findings.mitigation_adds: new frozen test (T-303); one CI step in job plugins; one gate question

findings.description: saveState writes '0,7' instead of '0.7'; loadState (correctly, by D-090) refuses the whole text because a value is not a finite number; the wrapper restores state only if loadState accepts it, so the session reopens with default parameters and no error. The user's sounds are lost silently.
findings.lens: technical correctness (state handling); operational (a user's DAW)
findings.conditions: the state text is written with printf-family %.9g (as D-090 literally says) or parsed with a locale-sensitive function, and the host process runs with a decimal-comma LC_NUMERIC (set by the host or by another plugin in the same process, a known occurrence on Linux hosts and some Windows hosts), or the session moves between machines with different locales
findings.root_cause: D-090 fixes the format by a printf conversion without fixing the locale; T-014 and T-302 run only in the C locale
findings.traces_to: D-090 (state text, %.9g), D-094 (restore only if accepted); T-014; T-302; S-ADVERSARIAL group 2 (tests decimal commas as input only)
findings.failure_path: T-014 round trip and T-302 round trip both run in the process default 'C' locale and pass; S-ADVERSARIAL feeds 'locale-style decimal commas' as malformed input and confirms refusal, which is the behaviour that destroys the session; no step runs saveState under a comma locale.
findings.mitigation: Amend D-090: values are formatted and parsed with std::to_chars / std::from_chars (locale-independent); add frozen test cases to T-014 and T-302 that call setlocale(LC_ALL, <a comma locale>) before saveState and loadState (CI generates de_DE.UTF-8 on Ubuntu; 'German' on Windows; failing to set the locale fails the test, never skips it).
findings.mitigation_adds: new frozen test cases (T-014c, T-302e); one line in ci.yml (locale-gen) and in ENVIRONMENT.md section 2

findings.description: D-094 exposes the factory presets as JUCE programs, and S-310 defines a preset as 'sets only the parameters named; everything else default'. If the host calls setCurrentProgram(k) after restoring the state, every parameter is reset to the preset and the restored state is overwritten. The current program is not part of the state text, so the wrapper cannot even tell that nothing changed.
findings.lens: technical correctness (state handling); operational (a user's DAW)
findings.conditions: a host restores the VST3 program-change parameter (which JUCE creates when getNumPrograms() > 1) or calls setCurrentProgram after setStateInformation, as some hosts do on session load
findings.root_cause: program selection and state restore interact in the VST3 wrapper; the plan specifies each in isolation
findings.traces_to: D-094 (programs), S-310 action 1 (factory.json semantics), D-090 (state text has no program field); T-302
findings.failure_path: T-302 restores a state and reads the parameters at once, with no program call; pluginval's state tests do not combine a program change with a restore; no step reopens a saved session in a real host. Sessions reload with factory sounds in an affected host.
findings.mitigation: Amend D-094: store the current program index in the state text (or in the JUCE wrapper's own chunk), make setCurrentProgram(i) a no-op when i is the current program, and never apply a program as part of a restore; add a frozen host test: set non-default values, save, restore into a fresh instance, call setCurrentProgram(getCurrentProgram()), and require every value unchanged; add a G-L gate question: save a Live set, close, reopen, does the sound survive?
findings.mitigation_adds: decision amendment; new frozen test case (T-302f); one gate question

findings.description: Engine::prepare is specified only for 44 100 to 96 000 Hz (engine.h). What the plugin does outside that range is undefined: an implementer following D-090's error style may throw std::invalid_argument from prepare (an exception through prepareToPlay crashes the host), clamp the rate internally (everything plays at the wrong pitch), or use the nearest reed-offset table (D-016) with a different sub-step count (tuning off by several cents).
findings.conditions: the owner opens a project at 192 kHz, 176.4 kHz, 32 kHz or 22.05 kHz (Ableton Live offers them)
findings.root_cause: A-009 states the supported range, but no decision says what happens outside it and no test reaches it
findings.traces_to: A-009; D-090; D-016 ('nearest listed rate'); core/include/folk/engine.h prepare(); T-160 (44.1, 48, 96 kHz only); S-ADVERSARIAL group 3 (44.1, 96, 88.2 kHz only)
findings.failure_path: Every test, the adversarial review and pluginval (default rates 44.1, 48 and 96 kHz) stay inside the range; S-310 and S-320 pass; the first 192 kHz session crashes the DAW (losing unsaved work) or plays out of tune.
findings.mitigation: Decide the behaviour in D-090 (for example: below 44.1 kHz or above 96 kHz the engine runs internally at the nearest supported rate behind a fixed resampler, or outputs silence and reports it in the editor; prepare never throws); add a frozen host test that calls prepareToPlay at 22 050, 32 000, 176 400 and 192 000 Hz, renders a note and requires no exception, finite output and either the documented silence or a pitch within 5 cents.
findings.mitigation_adds: decision amendment; new frozen test case (T-302g)

findings.description: D-094 lets getStateInformation push the JUCE values 'into the engine, or into a temporary engine off the audio thread'. The first reading mutates the live engine from the message thread while processBlock runs (a data race; a register, variant or moisture change rebuilds voice data). The other common way to satisfy 'never touches the engine while processBlock runs' is a lock taken on the audio thread. No test runs the wrapper concurrently, no sanitiser build covers the wrapper, and the host-style stress test the lessons require is a one-off engine-level attack in S-ADVERSARIAL, not a CI test.
findings.lens: technical correctness (real-time safety, threading); past lessons
findings.conditions: the implementer reads D-094's 'they are pushed into the engine' as the live audio engine, or guards processBlock and setStateInformation with a mutex
findings.root_cause: the decision text permits an unsafe option; lesson L-20261101T140000Z (host-style stress test in CI) and L-20261009T161100Z (what the audio thread locks) are applied to the core only
findings.traces_to: D-094; S-310 action 2; S-300 action 4 (ASan on folk-tests only); S-ADVERSARIAL group 3; PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE vst3-plugin group
findings.failure_path: T-302 calls getStateInformation and setStateInformation on one thread with no processing in flight; pluginval at strictness 10 is single-threaded for state calls; the ASan run covers the core; every Done when passes and the plugin crashes or glitches intermittently when a host saves (autosave) during playback.
findings.mitigation: Amend D-094 to allow only the temporary-engine route and forbid locks on the audio thread (parameters through atomics, state hand-over through a lock-free single-slot exchange); add a frozen host stress test that runs processBlock on one thread while another thread loops getStateInformation, setStateInformation and random parameter changes for 10 s, and a CI job that builds the host tests with -fsanitize=thread on ubuntu-24.04 and runs it.
findings.mitigation_adds: decision amendment; new frozen test (T-304); one CI job (TSan host tests)

findings.description: T-011's armed region calls setParam only with each parameter's default value, so a change never happens inside the allocation probe; T-009 changes parameters but checks only finiteness. Allocation on a structural parameter change in the audio thread is untested.
findings.lens: technical correctness (real-time safety; the tests themselves)
findings.conditions: a parameter change that alters structure (register, variant, key, body, range, moisture, course_mode) resizes or rebuilds a container in setParam or at the next block
findings.root_cause: the probe exercises setParam without changing state
findings.traces_to: tests/cpp/test_engine.cpp T-011 (setParam(..., def)); D-015; D-030 (register change while keys are held), D-040 (moisture), D-073 (variant)
findings.failure_path: An implementation that rebuilds the accordion rank list or the bouzouki course table with std::vector on a register or variant change passes T-011 (defaults only), T-009 (finite) and S-REVIEW unless the reviewer reads that path; automating 'register' in a DAW allocates on the audio thread and drops out under load.
findings.mitigation: Add a frozen T-011 case that, inside the armed region, sets every parameter to min, max and back while notes sound; or name the structural parameters in D-015 as preallocated in prepare().
findings.mitigation_adds: new frozen test case (T-011b)

findings.description: The frozen pass condition (at most 8 of 12 correct) passes when the listener fails to tell real from synthetic, so every way of not listening passes: chance answering passes with probability 0.93, all-'A' answers pass (side bias is only 'recorded'). A listener who hears the difference 70 % of the time passes a round with probability 0.51 and within the three allowed rounds with 0.88; at 80 % it is 0.21 and 0.50. Harmonica, melodion and bouzouki have no pairs at all and pass on one line, 'wrong: none'. R-011's mitigation (and R-005's, R-002's, R-004's) rests on these gates.
findings.lens: integrity (listening scores); technical correctness (could every check pass while the product is wrong)
findings.conditions: the candidate is distinguishable but not trivially so (a listener right about 70 % of the time), or the listener is inattentive, uses laptop speakers, or answers with a side bias
findings.root_cause: an equivalence claim is tested with a low-power difference test whose null result counts as success, and with no check that the listener is discriminating at all
findings.traces_to: D-053; plan/GATES.md G-L1 to G-L5; S-LISTEN Done when; A-011; HANDOFF.md section 9; lesson L-20261106T180300Z (12 pairs too noisy)
findings.failure_path: S-LISTEN Done when requires only a recorded proceed with a score of 8 or fewer; an inattentive or merely moderately discriminating listener produces such a score, the gate records proceed, S-INTEGRATE opens the pull request, and the instruments ship sounding synthetic, with 'passed blind listening' in the records.
findings.mitigation: Add two control pairs per round in which the candidate is the reference itself low-passed at 2 kHz or with its attack removed (a difference any attentive listener hears); a round in which a control pair is missed, or one letter is given for 10 or more pairs, is void and repeated with a new seed, not passed; raise the pairs to 20 with the pass condition 'at most 13 of 20' or state plainly in the gate record that the score is evidence only of indistinguishability at the 0.07 level; forbid counting a void round against the round limit.
findings.mitigation_adds: amendment of D-053 and GATES.md (frozen pass condition, set before any listening, so no listening result is relaxed); a change to tools/build_evidence.py (control pairs); a step check in S-LISTEN

findings.description: The seed is the round number (seed=1 for every round 1) and appears in the marker commit and in the evidence commit message; make_blind_pairs.py draws the sides from random.Random(seed) over the sorted stems, so the answer key is computable from public data before the listener answers. The key itself ships, only base64-encoded, in the same zip as the pairs.
findings.conditions: anyone, the implementing agent included, reruns the public deterministic pair builder with the seed in the marker commit, or opens key.json.b64 in the downloaded zip
findings.root_cause: blindness rests on obscurity
findings.traces_to: S-LISTEN action 1 (seed = round number); plan/ci/gate-evidence.yml (message carries the seed); tools/listening/make_blind_pairs.py; HANDOFF.md section 9
findings.failure_path: Nothing checks that the key stayed unknown; a leaked hint ('pair 3 is the real one') or a curious decode passes the gate with any score the hint allows.
findings.mitigation: Draw the seed from a secret generated per round and kept outside the repository (commit only its sha256 in the gate record); keep key.json.b64 and sources.json.b64 out of the delivered zip (store them with the private pairs or encrypt them to the implementer); reveal the seed after scoring.
findings.mitigation_adds: step change in S-LISTEN and tools/build_evidence.py; no frozen test

findings.description: DR-07 fits three 6-point curves over pitch (18 free values) against T-200, which compares 17 pitches of the same TinySOL notes; the G-L3 pairs use 12 notes of the same recordings. Calibration on the test data makes T-200 a fit residual rather than a check, and the listening pairs are cut from the very recordings the model was fitted to.
findings.lens: integrity (tests bypassed by calibration); invalid research assumptions
findings.conditions: S-330 calibrates (DR-07)
findings.root_cause: no hold-out between calibration data and validation data
findings.traces_to: DR-07; D-012 (6-point curves); S-330; tests/py/test_reference.py (PITCHES 45..93 step 3 with neighbours); D-050; G-L3
findings.failure_path: S-330 Done when is 'the reference tests pass after at most five rounds'; a fit that matches 17 notes passes T-200 while the notes between them (and every other register) drift; G-L3 then compares the fitted notes with their own recordings.
findings.mitigation: Split TinySOL in D-050: calibrate on pp and ff or on the even semitones, validate T-200 and the G-L3 pairs on held-out notes; limit each curve to 3 points.
findings.mitigation_adds: decision amendment; T-200 amendment (pitch subset) before the freeze is re-cut

findings.description: D-050 fixes the candidate patch at register 1 (Clarinet, one rank) and DR-07 calibrates the shared reed curves until that single rank matches the recordings. If the recordings contain a detuned or 16-foot rank, calibration distorts the reed itself to imitate a register mix, and every register of the product inherits the distortion.
findings.conditions: the TinySOL accordion was recorded in a register other than a single 8-foot rank (C-021: 'the register of the recorded accordion is not stated'; C-055: about one note in ten shows a component an octave below)
findings.root_cause: a load-bearing comparison rests on an unstated property of the dataset
findings.failure_path: T-200 passes after calibration; the Musette and Master registers then double the distortion; the listening gate (finding 7) does not catch it.
findings.mitigation: Add a spike before S-330 (or a check in S-REF): measure beating (amplitude modulation at 0.5 to 15 Hz) and sub-octave energy in the 12 G-L3 notes and the T-200 notes, record the inferred ranks as a claim, and amend the candidate patch if it is not one 8-foot rank.
findings.mitigation_adds: one spike or step check; possibly a D-050 amendment

findings.description: C-051 (single-source, load-bearing) says no redistributable isolated notes exist for harmonica, melodica or mandolin, but Freesound, the largest source of CC0 and CC BY single notes, 'could not be searched'. S-REF's bounded search omits it, and no gate question asks the owner for own recordings or a Freesound pack, so R-005's mitigation ('the bounded search in S-REF'; 'the owner may add own recordings through iterate') is never triggered.
findings.conditions: none beyond the plan as written
findings.root_cause: the search list was set by what the planning sandbox could reach
findings.traces_to: C-051; D-051; S-REF action 3; G-P1, G-P2, G-L1, G-L4 questions; R-005
findings.failure_path: S-REF Done when passes with nothing found for harmonica and melodion; G-L1 and G-L4 run on demos only and pass on 'wrong: none'.
findings.mitigation: Add Freesound to S-REF (API with a credential requested at G-P1, or the owner downloads named packs at G-P1), with the same licence and creator rules; add a question to G-P1 and G-P2: 'Can you supply recordings of your own or name a source?'
findings.mitigation_adds: step change in S-REF; one gate question

findings.description: D-052 has the shared ci.yml fetch every indexed reference, private Philharmonia notes included, on every push to main and every pull request, for the life of the repository. R-014's mitigation is that S-REVIEW checks the workflows once; it does not cover a fork's pull request, which runs its own modified ci.yml and may upload refs/ as an artifact of a run in the owner's repository, nor any edit after delivery.
findings.lens: licensing; security (supply chain of the workflow)
findings.conditions: a pull request from a fork (workflows of outside contributors run without approval for accounts that are not new to GitHub, by the default setting) or a later maintenance edit adds an upload or cache of refs/ to ci.yml
findings.root_cause: private material is fetched by a shared, public, long-lived workflow rather than on demand
findings.traces_to: D-052; plan/ci/ci.yml job reference (lines 183-184); R-014; Rule 15 (c), (d)
findings.failure_path: The workflow as planned passes S-REVIEW; six months later a contributor's pull request adds 'uses: actions/upload-artifact with path: refs' for debugging; the run executes without approval and publishes the Philharmonia mandolin files from the owner's repository.
findings.mitigation: Run the private part of T-201 only in a workflow triggered by workflow_dispatch on impl-** branches (or locally, DR-13), and make ci.yml's reference job pass --only-redistributable on main and pull requests; record as a G-002-style owner action the Actions setting 'Require approval for all outside collaborators'.
findings.mitigation_adds: workflow change (ci.yml plus a private-reference workflow); an owner setting recorded in S-INTEGRATE

findings.description: all-green on main depends on hosts and data outside the project's control: the reference job downloads the 1 GB TinySOL archive whenever the 7-day cache is evicted and fetches Philharmonia files from S3 (link rot, rate limits, terms changes: DR-11); pip-audit --strict turns red on any new advisory for numpy, scipy, soundfile or pytest (DR-08); runner images change Xcode and MSVC weekly; transitive Python dependencies are unpinned. The rules that handle each are written for the implementer, who has gone; no owner-facing note says what to do.
findings.conditions: six months of unattended time after merge
findings.root_cause: delivery-time gates are kept as permanent required checks with no maintenance procedure
findings.traces_to: plan/ci/ci.yml (reference, audit, all-green); DR-02, DR-08, DR-11; D-005; R-006; A-018 ('hobby; best effort')
findings.failure_path: Every Done when passed at delivery; within months main is red for reasons unrelated to the code, so a real regression is indistinguishable from drift, and a branch protection on all-green blocks every fix.
findings.mitigation: Add to README a maintenance section (one line per job: why it can go red without a code change, and the rule to apply); keep build and test jobs required, and move reference and audit to a schedule plus impl/pr branches with failures reported as issues rather than blocking main; hash-lock the transitive Python dependencies.
findings.mitigation_adds: documentation; workflow triggers; a lock file

findings.description: The gate-evidence job runs with permissions contents: write; actions/checkout persists that token in .git/config by default; the job then pip-installs requirements whose transitive dependencies are unpinned and unhashed and runs repository tools and pytest. Any code in that chain can push to main, rewrite tags or replace evidence branches.
findings.conditions: one transitive Python dependency (pluggy, iniconfig, packaging, pygments, cffi, pycparser) is compromised on PyPI during the project's life, while main has no branch protection (D-006: none at planning)
findings.root_cause: write permission granted to the whole job; dependencies pinned only at the top level
findings.traces_to: plan/ci/gate-evidence.yml (permissions, checkout, pip install); tests/requirements.txt; plan/ENVIRONMENT.md section 1 ('their own dependencies are resolved by pip at install time'); D-006
findings.failure_path: S-003, S-210 and S-340 pass with the workflow as written; nothing checks credential scope or dependency hashes; a malicious post-install or import-time payload in a transitive package uses the persisted token.
findings.mitigation: Hash-lock all Python dependencies (pip-compile --generate-hashes; pip install --require-hashes) in both workflows; set persist-credentials: false on checkout and expose the token only to the push step (or move the push into a second job that only checks out nothing and pushes the built directory); ask the owner to protect main at S-INTEGRATE.
findings.mitigation_adds: workflow change; a lock file; an owner setting

findings.description: D-052 tells fetch_references.py to download source_url and 'extract the member named by file'; the URLs come from search results, not from the plan. On Python 3.13 tarfile without a filter follows the fully trusted behaviour. A crafted archive can write outside the reference root, for example over tools/evidence_guard.py or tools/build_evidence.py in the CI checkout before they run in gate-evidence (which holds a write token).
findings.conditions: an archive indexed from a search result (Zenodo or archive.org, S-REF sources b and c) contains members with '..', absolute paths or links, and fetch_references.py extracts with tarfile or zipfile defaults
findings.root_cause: the extraction contract does not say how to treat untrusted archive members
findings.traces_to: D-052; S-REF action 5; plan/ci/ci.yml and gate-evidence.yml (fetch before build_evidence); Rule 16
findings.failure_path: T-210 tests the guard, not the fetcher; S-REF Done when checks that the fetch exits 0 and the hashes match (the hash is of the extracted member, not of the archive); a path-traversal member lands without any check failing.
findings.mitigation: Amend D-052: record and check the archive's own sha256 before extraction; extract only the one named member with tarfile filter='data' (zipfile: reject names with '..' or a leading '/'), never links; add a frozen test of fetch_references.py with a crafted archive (member '../x', absolute member, symlink) that must exit non-zero and write nothing outside the root.
findings.mitigation_adds: decision amendment; new frozen test (T-211)

findings.description: S-KNOW clones the stores at their current head and runs 'each store's own python scripts/build_index.py and python scripts/check_knowledge_schema.py' with the push credential available, without pinning them to the commits read in R0 (9934bb5, f3d176d) and without reading them. A repository's files are untrusted content under Rule 16.
findings.conditions: the store's scripts changed after R0 (another run, an agent, or a compromise)
findings.root_cause: store infrastructure is treated as trusted code
findings.traces_to: S-KNOW action 2; A-015; Rule 16 (repositories are untrusted)
findings.failure_path: G-003 answered push-to-proposed; S-KNOW clones, runs the scripts, pushes; Done when checks only that the indexes list the IDs, which a hostile script can also arrange.
findings.mitigation: Before running them, diff each store's scripts/ against the commit read in R0 and stop with BLOCKED.md if they differ (or read the diff line by line as for 1.3.6 commands); run them in a process without the credential and push in a separate command.
findings.mitigation_adds: step check in S-KNOW

findings.description: S-REVIEW says 'Fix every Critical and High finding', but its Outputs allow 'either the fix commit or an R-### entry ... with the reason for accepting it' for every finding, and its Done when says only 'no Critical or High finding is open'. An accepted risk is not 'open'. S-ADVERSARIAL has the same pattern ('an accepted R-### with severity'). The implementer, whose code was reviewed, writes the register entry.
findings.conditions: a Critical or High finding is hard to fix
findings.root_cause: closure by acceptance is not restricted by severity or by who accepts
findings.traces_to: S-REVIEW Outputs and Done when; S-ADVERSARIAL Outputs and Done when; premortem/RISK_REGISTER.md status values
findings.failure_path: A Critical security finding is entered as 'R-0xx accepted: hobby project'; Done when holds; S-LISTEN and S-INTEGRATE proceed; the pull request lists the review as clean of open Critical findings.
findings.mitigation: Done when of both steps: every Critical and High has a fix commit verified by the fresh-context reviewer; acceptance of a Critical or High only by the owner at a gate (a G-REVIEW record), never by the implementer; Medium and Low may be accepted as R-### by the reviewer.
findings.mitigation_adds: step change in S-REVIEW and S-ADVERSARIAL; one gate (only when needed)

findings.description: DR-16 lets the pull request open with the reference job red and says the step is done 'when every other check is green'. all-green needs reference, so all-green is red too, and all-green is the one check D-005 and ENVIRONMENT.md section 5 tell the owner to require. The implementer must guess whether a red all-green is allowed; after merge main is red permanently and a protection on all-green blocks every later pull request.
findings.conditions: S-330 ends failed under DR-07 and the owner answers proceed-with-rescope
findings.root_cause: the exception rule names one red check but the aggregator inherits it
findings.traces_to: DR-16; S-INTEGRATE Done when ('none failing'); plan/ci/ci.yml all-green; plan/ENVIRONMENT.md section 5
findings.failure_path: S-INTEGRATE's Done when ('every check on its head commit is green') contradicts DR-16; either the implementer halts (blocked) or reads DR-16 as overriding and delivers a pull request whose required check fails.
findings.mitigation: State in DR-16 that all-green is the second permitted red check; have the pull request description say that main will stay red until the named shortfall is fixed, and record the owner's choice (merge red, or keep the instrument's reference test out of the required set by an amendment).
findings.mitigation_adds: decision rule amendment

findings.description: D-084 estimates 150 runner-minutes per push but omits GitHub's billing multipliers for private repositories (Windows 2x, macOS 10x). With two macOS plugin jobs of 20 to 35 minutes and two macOS core jobs, one push costs roughly 800 billed minutes against a monthly quota of 2 000 (Free) or 3 000 (Pro). The plan pushes after every step, and every marker commit runs ci.yml as well; cancelled runs are still billed.
findings.lens: operational realities; past lessons (L-20261107T213402Z, quota arithmetic)
findings.conditions: the repository is private (the plan does not know: D-007, HANDOFF.md section 9) on a Free or Pro plan
findings.root_cause: the budget arithmetic of the lesson was done in wall minutes, not billed minutes, and visibility was never probed
findings.traces_to: D-084; D-007; S-000 action 5 (visibility not probed); PUSH convention; lesson L-20261107T213402Z
findings.failure_path: S-003 passes on the first run; a few pushes later Actions refuses to start jobs; S-320 cannot be reached; the implementer halts mid-plan (blocked) or the owner pays unexpectedly.
findings.mitigation: S-000 records repository visibility and the Actions quota; D-084 computes billed minutes; if private, ci.yml runs the macOS and Windows jobs only on workflow_dispatch and on commits carrying a marker (S-003, S-320, S-INTEGRATE), with Linux core on every push, and the owner confirms the budget at a gate before S-003.
findings.mitigation_adds: S-000 check; workflow trigger change; one gate

findings.description: C-048 verified the Python pins only on the Linux sandbox. The core job installs tests/requirements.txt before configuring, on all four runners; without a wheel pip builds scipy from source, which fails without a Fortran toolchain.
findings.conditions: numpy 2.5.3 or scipy 1.18.1 has no cp313 wheel for macOS x86_64 (macos-15-intel) or Windows x64
findings.root_cause: pins checked on one platform of four
findings.traces_to: C-048; D-085; plan/ci/ci.yml core job step 'Python packages'; S-003 Done when (core must reach its test step on all four runners)
findings.failure_path: S-003 cannot meet its Done when on that runner; DR-01 halts the plan with BLOCKED.md.
findings.mitigation: At planning, run 'pip download --only-binary=:all: --platform <tag> --python-version 3.13' for macosx x86_64, macosx arm64 and win_amd64 for each pin and record the result in ENVIRONMENT.md section 5 with a pre-decided fallback (the nearest version that has all wheels).
findings.mitigation_adds: a planning check; a row in ENVIRONMENT.md section 5

findings.description: D-016 and D-033 give exact RMS formulas for the breath noise and the key noise, but T-109 and T-125 assert only lower bounds (at least 6 dB more energy in a band). A noise stage 20 dB louder than intended passes.
findings.lens: past lessons (L-20261009T120012Z, stochastic stage power); the tests themselves
findings.conditions: the breath or key noise is implemented at the wrong level (for example S_ref taken at the wrong rate or before the wrong gain)
findings.root_cause: the lesson's rule (output power per band equals an independently computed intended power) was applied as 'the noise is audible'
findings.traces_to: D-016 (air_noise RMS), D-033 key noise; T-109, T-125; PRIOR_KNOWLEDGE dsp-correctness group
findings.failure_path: PY harmonica, accordion and melodion pass; the default air_noise of 0.2 hisses; only the listener can notice, through the weak gate of finding 7.
findings.mitigation: Add a frozen test comparing the noise band (between harmonics) at air_noise 0.2 and 1.0: the ratio is 14 dB within 1 dB, and the absolute RMS is within 3 dB of the D-016 formula (S_ref and vj_mean printed by an extended --dump-model for reeds); the same for key_noise against D-033.
findings.mitigation_adds: new frozen test case (T-109b)

findings.description: G_out is calibrated so that one default note in the default register peaks at -12 dBFS. Four ranks add about 6 dB and a four-note chord another 6 dB, so normal chords drive the tanh limiter near full scale, where it distorts audibly; no test or check bounds the level of chords or the true peak of the plugin's output.
findings.lens: technical correctness (gain staging); past lessons (L-20261009T090804Z, true peak)
findings.conditions: the accordion is played in the Master register (four ranks) or with chords, or the melodion and harmonica with chords, at normal velocity
findings.root_cause: gain calibrated on one note; the limiter is treated as a safety net, not budgeted
findings.traces_to: D-013, D-015; GAIN convention; T-009 (peak at most 1, which tanh guarantees); T-124; demos -06-chords
findings.failure_path: All tests pass (T-124 checks only that 16 keys sound); demos of chords sound saturated; the listener may or may not attribute it.
findings.mitigation: Normalise the accordion's rank sum by the number of active ranks (or calibrate G_out per register); add a frozen test that a four-note chord in Master at velocity 0.8 peaks below -3 dBFS before the limiter, and make build_evidence fail if any demo's true peak exceeds -1 dBFS.
findings.mitigation_adds: decision amendment; new frozen test case; a check in build_evidence

findings.description: D-060 fixes the number of partials at the stroke (those below 18 kHz). The pitch wheel then raises every partial by up to an octave (bend_range 12) without removing those that cross the Nyquist frequency, so they fold back as inharmonic tones.
findings.conditions: bend_range above about 3 semitones and the wheel moved up on mid or high notes at 44.1 or 48 kHz
findings.root_cause: the partial budget is computed once per stroke
findings.traces_to: D-060, D-062 (control-tick recomputation), D-091 bend_range 0 to 12; T-150 (checks only the fundamental's shift)
findings.failure_path: T-150 passes at bend_range 12 because it measures the peak near 880 Hz; an upward bend on the E course aliases audibly.
findings.mitigation: At each control tick zero the partials whose bent frequency exceeds min(18 kHz, 0.45 fs); add a frozen test: bend +12 on MIDI 88 at 44.1 kHz, energy outside the harmonic series at least 60 dB below the fundamental.
findings.mitigation_adds: decision amendment; new frozen test case (T-150b)

findings.description: R = 4 is fixed, so at 96 kHz the base rate is 384 kHz and most reeds need one sub-step, roughly twice the per-reed cost at 48 kHz. T-013 measures only 48 kHz, where the margin is already thin (C-054: 5.6 times for reeds alone; target 4).
findings.conditions: the owner works at 88.2 or 96 kHz (A-009 says supported) with the accordion in Master and full chords
findings.root_cause: performance target named for one rate while a range is supported
findings.traces_to: A-009; D-011, D-014; T-013; R-007 (48 kHz on the CI runner only)
findings.failure_path: T-013 passes on ubuntu-24.04 at 48 kHz; at 96 kHz on a typical laptop core the accordion runs near or below real time and drops out.
findings.mitigation: Make the base rate depend on the host rate (R = 4 at 44.1 and 48 kHz, R = 2 at 88.2 and 96 kHz, decimator stages to match) or add a gating 96 kHz case to T-013 with a stated factor (for example 2.5) and DR-06 applied to it.
findings.mitigation_adds: decision amendment or new frozen test case (T-013b)

findings.description: Standalone is a declared format (A-005, SC-01), built in CI, and never started by any test or step.
findings.conditions: a Standalone-specific defect (audio device set-up, MIDI input, window creation)
findings.root_cause: host tests compile the processor, pluginval loads the VST3
findings.traces_to: A-005; SC-01; plugins/CMakeLists.txt FORMATS VST3 Standalone; plan/ci/ci.yml plugins job
findings.failure_path: S-310 and S-320 pass; the Standalone crashes at start.
findings.mitigation: Start each Standalone with a timeout under xvfb on Linux (and directly on macOS and Windows) and require it to stay alive for 5 s and quit cleanly.
findings.mitigation_adds: one CI step

findings.description: No step installs a plugin in the assumed host (A-005: Ableton Live). The only binaries are CI artifacts with 3-day retention, so after merge none exist; the macOS bundles are not signed (out of scope) and a downloaded bundle carries the quarantine attribute, which Gatekeeper blocks; the README is not required to say how to install or unblock them.
findings.conditions: the owner installs the plugins after merge
findings.root_cause: delivery ends at a green pull request; the user's first contact with the plugin is unplanned
findings.traces_to: A-005, A-018; D-007 (retention 3 days); S-INTEGRATE; plan/ci/ci.yml upload step
findings.failure_path: Every Done when passes; six months later the owner has no binary, rebuilds or re-runs CI, and on macOS Live does not load the bundles.
findings.mitigation: Add an ad-hoc codesign step for the macOS bundles in CI and README install notes (paths per OS, unquarantine command); add one owner check at G-L1 (load the plugin from the gate's CI artifact in the assumed host, play, save and reopen) so that host-level failures (findings 1 to 4) surface before integration.
findings.mitigation_adds: one CI step; README section; one gate question

findings.description: D-090 refuses a state text with an unknown key as a whole, and the header carries a version number with no migration rule. Any evolution of the parameter table therefore resets every affected session to defaults.
findings.conditions: any later version renames or removes a parameter, or a session saved by a newer build is opened by an older one
findings.root_cause: strictness chosen for security without a compatibility path
findings.traces_to: D-090; T-014 (refusal of 'no_such_param=1' is frozen)
findings.failure_path: Not visible at delivery; the first parameter change after delivery loses users' settings silently.
findings.mitigation: Amend D-090: unknown keys are ignored (counted, not applied) while malformed lines still refuse the text; define 'folk-state 2' migration as a table; this needs a T-014 amendment.
findings.mitigation_adds: decision amendment; frozen test amendment (T-014)

findings.description: (a) CC BY 4.0 requires stating that TinySOL clips were modified (cut, resampled, level-normalised); ATTRIBUTION.md is specified with author, title, URL, licence and citation only. (b) CC BY-SA material (the Wikimedia bouzouki notes) would require derived clips to carry CC BY-SA; the evidence branch states no licence. (c) tools/listening is Apache-2.0 without the licence text in the repository. (d) The binary artifacts include only the AGPL LICENSE, not the VST3 SDK's MIT notice.
findings.lens: licensing of reference audio and published evidence
findings.conditions: none
findings.root_cause: attribution specified as a list, not against each licence's conditions
findings.traces_to: S-REF action 4; S-340 (ATTRIBUTION.md); D-053, D-081; plan/ci/ci.yml 'Collect the five VST3 bundles'
findings.failure_path: T-210 and the guard check redistributability, not licence conditions; every Done when passes.
findings.mitigation: Specify ATTRIBUTION.md per licence (changes made; ShareAlike licence for derived clips); add LICENSE-APACHE beside tools/listening and the VST3 SDK and JUCE notices to the artifact.
findings.mitigation_adds: documentation; one CI copy line

findings.description: T-201's threshold is max(6 dB, the 90th percentile of the set's own neighbour spread), computed from whatever S-REF indexed. A heterogeneous set raises its own threshold so far that any candidate passes; with fewer than 8 notes the test prints NOT-APPLICABLE and passes.
findings.conditions: the reference set mixes dynamics, articulations or recording set-ups (Philharmonia mandolin files include several of each), or the implementer adds such notes
findings.root_cause: a self-referential threshold over a set chosen by the implementer
findings.traces_to: tests/py/test_reference.py T-201b; S-REF action 4 (usable-note rule); D-051
findings.failure_path: S-330 Done when ('pytest -m reference exits 0') passes for the mandolin with a wide limit; G-L2 then rests on the weak gate of finding 7.
findings.mitigation: Restrict indexed notes per instrument to one articulation and one dynamic band (recorded in the row), print the limit with the comparison in METRICS.md, and cap the limit (for example 10 dB, the largest TinySOL figure) by amendment of T-201.
findings.mitigation_adds: S-REF rule; frozen test amendment (T-201b)

findings.description: The plugins job runs 'ctest --test-dir build -C Release --output-on-failure -E folk-perf'; ctest exits 0 when it finds no tests unless --no-tests=error is given. The CI job does not check how many tests ran, and S-320's Done when reads pluginval lines and PERF lines, not the host-test count.
findings.lens: CI platform coverage; integrity (a verification that reported success without having run)
findings.conditions: a CMake change leaves the host tests unregistered on one runner (for example add_test moved under a condition or a generator-specific path)
findings.root_cause: exit status taken as proof of coverage for ctest (knowledge K-20261104T005300Z warns of exactly this for pluginval)
findings.traces_to: plan/ci/ci.yml plugins 'Host tests'; S-320 Done when; T-302
findings.failure_path: On that runner 'No tests were found' and the step is green; T-302 never ran there; S-320 passes.
findings.mitigation: Use 'ctest --no-tests=error' and assert the summary line reports exactly 6 tests (five HostTests and folk-tests) in the step.
findings.mitigation_adds: CI step change

findings.description: C-056 shows an idealised additive stand-in passes every Python behaviour test. The checks that tie the product to the physical model (S-200's reed_probe offsets and amplitude, S-201's table) run through reed_probe, an implementer-written program that is required to 'run one reed of the core' but is not required to use the same code path as Engine::process.
findings.conditions: T-013 is tight and the implementer optimises the engine path separately from reed_probe
findings.root_cause: the model's identity is verified through a side tool
findings.traces_to: C-056; S-200 Done when; S-201; DR-06 ('optimise without changing the model')
findings.failure_path: Under DR-06 pressure the voice is made cheaper in the engine only; reed_probe still reproduces S12; all Done when pass; S-REVIEW may not notice.
findings.mitigation: Require reed_probe to drive the reed through the same Reed class and step function the engine uses (S-REVIEW checks it), and add a frozen test that renders one note through folk-render at the reed_probe operating point and compares pitch offset and harmonic levels with reed_probe's output.
findings.mitigation_adds: step check; new frozen test case

findings.description: S-210 and S-250 tell the implementer to 'paste into the record by hand' the list of passing frozen tests and the PERF lines (at S-210 the local, not CI, figures, for instruments that are still silent).
findings.conditions: a transcription error
findings.root_cause: hand transcription
findings.traces_to: S-210 gate actions (6); S-250 gate actions
findings.failure_path: The owner decides G-P1 on a typed list; nothing checks it.
findings.mitigation: Generate the list from the junit and pytest reports with a script and commit its output; quote the CI PERF lines with the run URL.
findings.mitigation_adds: step change

findings.description: m = ceil(C f_r / (R fs)) gives at least 110 steps per period; divergence starts at about 95 at 1500 Pa (C-060). Raising a4_hz from 415 to 466 Hz mid-note lowers the steps per period by 12 % if m is not recomputed. D-015 then resets the voice silently, so the tests (finite output) still pass.
findings.conditions: a4_hz automated upwards while a low reed sounds, and the sub-step count m of D-011 kept from note-on
findings.root_cause: D-011 does not say when m is recomputed
findings.failure_path: speculative: depends on an implementation choice D-011 leaves open; no frozen test changes a4_hz during a note at full vibrato.
findings.mitigation: State in D-011 that m is recomputed whenever f_r changes.
findings.mitigation_adds: decision clarification

findings.description: Review of the load-bearing single-source claims found no new failure path: the C-012 bend depths, the overbend holes and the chromatic layout of C-014 agree with the standard Richter and solo-tuned layouts; the C-017 footages are the usual ones; C-039's trichordo course octaves remain Tier 3 only. The failure path is R-001's. Its mitigation ('the owner hears every variant at the gates') is weakened by finding 7, and a non-player owner may not recognise a wrong bend depth.
findings.lens: invalid research assumptions (C-012, C-013, C-014, C-017, C-039)
findings.conditions: one table detail is wrong
findings.root_cause: no Tier 1 source read
findings.failure_path: as R-001
findings.mitigation: none beyond R-001 and finding 7
findings.mitigation_adds: none

findings.description: S-REF says a find under any other licence 'is indexed only for the mandolin under D-051 (source (d))'; it is unclear whether a non-Philharmonia mandolin find under a restrictive licence may be indexed as private. D-051 justifies only Philharmonia.
findings.conditions: S-REF finds a mandolin note under a non-commercial or Sampling Plus licence at source (a), (b) or (c)
findings.root_cause: ambiguous parenthesis
findings.traces_to: S-REF action 4; D-051
findings.failure_path: The implementer indexes it as private without a D-### justification, contrary to Rule 15's requirement; nothing checks that each private row has a justifying decision.
findings.mitigation: Say explicitly: only Philharmonia rows may be private; any other restrictive find is recorded as 'not used'.
findings.mitigation_adds: wording

summary: 35 findings: 31 new, 3 residual, 1 restated; severity 7 Critical, 8 High, 16 Medium, 4 Low; 1 speculative. The central failure: every audio check and gate exercises folk-render and the core, never the shipped VST3 in a host, and the listening gates pass whenever the listener does not discriminate; state handling (locale, program change) can lose sessions silently.
